value.text:
The University of Ljubljana (Slovene: Univerza v Ljubljani; Latin: Universitas Labacensis) is a public university based in Ljubljana, Slovenia. Its teaching and research span the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, technology, the arts and health-related fields. The university's central building is in Congress Square, while its faculties and other facilities extend across the city. The institution also lists Portorož among its locations.

The current university was established in 1919, following efforts to create a Slovene-language university. Its founding legislation passed in July that year, a university council was constituted in September, and lectures began in December. The initial institution had five faculties: law, philosophy, technology, theology and medicine. Ljubljana had previously hosted a French-administered university founded in 1810 and dissolved in 1813; that earlier institution should not be confused with the university founded in 1919. The present institution was renamed for Edvard Kardelj in 1979 and restored its original name in 1990.

An encyclopedia account describes 23 faculties and three art academies as of 2018, encompassing a range of disciplines, and reports approximately 38,000 enrolled students without a clear statistical year. These figures are indicative of the scale described by the source, rather than current audited counts.
